[[Lord Exo]]'s Followers (Formerly) |first_appearance = [[Null & Void Event]] }} ==Description== The '''Old World''' was the first realm to exist in the story of Tower Defense Simulator. It is unknown whether the realm has existed eternally, or was created. A plethora of living beings called the '''Old World''' their home, none more prominent than [[Two X]] and [[Lord Exo]], who shared power in the realm.{{InlineQuote|Long ago, two brothers ruled over all creation. Each saw the Old World as a blank canvas, but like any artist, each viewed the world much differently.|[[Narrator (Narrator)|Narrator]] on Wave 2 ([[The Narratorium]])}} The aftermath of [[Two X]] and [[Lord Exo]]'s war in the '''Old World''' turned the realm into a hazardous and uninhabitable landscape.{{InlineQuote|Now that [[Lord Exo]] was defeated, [[Two X]] was left with an uninhabitable wasteland that became the Nil Zone!|[[Narrator (Narrator)|Narrator]] on Wave 20 ([[The Narratorium]])}} Its original inhabitants migrated to Paradise after the war.{{InlineQuote|Leaving the [[Old World]] behind, everyone started making a new home that [[Two X]] had always envisioned.|[[Narrator (Narrator)|Narrator]] on Wave 21 ([[The Narratorium]])}} ==Inhabitants== [[Two X]] and [[Lord Exo]] can be considered one of the first, if not the first beings to inhabit the '''Old World'''. The governed over their own sides of the '''Old World''', but eventually fell into conflict with one another over opposing views of how creation should be treated, resulting in the war.{{InlineQuote|You see, [[Two X]] believed everyone had a place in the world, so he helped nurture them. Meanwhile, [[Lord Exo]] created creatures as tall as buildings while wiping out thousands that didn't suit his vision.|[[Narrator (Narrator)|Narrator]] on Wave 5 ([[The Narratorium]])}} The [[Rift Walker (Story)|Rift Walker]] and the [[Narrator (Story)|Narrator]] are two beings that originate from the '''Old World''', they both seem to serve as right-hand men for their respective masters. The [[Rift Walker (Story)|Rift Walker]] helped [[Two X]] create the [[Meta]] after the war, but it is unknown what his activities before and during the war were. Before the war, the [[Narrator (Story)|Narrator]] was a performer{{InlineQuote|The [[Narrator (Story)|Narrator]] is a performer from the '''Old World''' who used to be the right-hand man of [[Lord Exo]].|[[Narrator (Enemy)|Narrator]]'s description in its [[Logbooks|Logbook]]}} and self described "''artist'',"{{InlineQuote|COMEDIAN? I am a PERFORMER! An ARTIST! A DIRECTOR!|[[Narrator (Narrator)|Narrator]] on Wave 22 ([[Banlands]])}} aside from this, he helped instigate [[Lord Exo]]'s freedom from the [[God Cube]]. The [[Null Guardian (Story)|Null Guardian]] inhabits the [[Banlands|Outer Nil Zone]], but whether he originated from the '''Old World''' is unknown, as it is likely he could have been sent there by the [[Rift Walker (Story)|Rift Walker]] after the creation of the [[Meta]].{{InlineQuote|The [[Null Guardian (Story)|Null Guardian]] has existed within the Nil Zone since before the '''Old World''', appointed to this role by the [[Rift Walker (Story)|Rift Walker]] himself.|[[Null Guardian]]'s description in its [[Logbooks|Logbook]]}} Myriads of other living beings also populated the '''Old World''', such as [[Two X]] and [[Lord Exo]]'s respective followers and creations. Although the [[Narrator (Story)|Narrator]] refers to the [[Banlands|Nil Zone]] as an uninhabitable wasteland that was left by everyone, the [[Null & Void Event]] enemy [[Logbooks]] point to this not being entirely the case, as it is suggested through them that the [[Banlands|Nil Zone]] contains its own ecosystem of species, some enemies even evolving from other enemies.{{InlineQuote|It relentlessly hunts [[Null Runner]]s, who have learned to run at the sight of it. The creature's very existence appears to cause it pain, as it evolved from the same thing that it hunts.|[[Lost Glitch]]'s description in its [[Logbooks|Logbook]]}} One such enemy, the [[Null Beast]], is used by the [[Narrator (Story)|Narrator]] to represent [[Lord Exo]]'s followers[[File:CardboardMonsters.png|280px]]
[[File:CardboardExoCrowdAngry.png|280px]], which implies some of these entities used to live in the '''Old World'''. This in turn suggests that when it turned into the Nil Zone, they for unknown reasons chose to or could not leave it for Paradise. ==Locations== ===Nil Zone=== {{LocationInfobox |title = Nil Zone |image = |-|Outer Nil Zone = [[File:Nilzone.jpg]] |-|Temple of Exo = [[File:Templeofexo.jpg]] |purpose = Prison for entities that pose a threat to the [[Meta]] |inhabitants = The [[Null Guardian]] (Warden)
[[Corrupted Titus|Titus]] (Detainee) }} The [[T.D.S. Organization]]'s first encounter with the '''Old World''' was through the [[Banlands|Nil Zone]], after a group of their agents was banished there by the [[Rift Walker (Story)|Rift Walker]]. The [[Banlands|Nil Zone]] is all that remains of the '''Old World''' after the war.{{InlineQuote|Wait, we were in the '''Old World'''?!|[[Commander (Narrator)|Commander]] on Wave 20 ([[The Narratorium]])}}
{{InlineQuote|Ha! What's left of it!|[[Narrator (Narrator)|Narrator]] on Wave 20 ([[The Narratorium]])}} The region takes the form of a purple and black wasteland, with sharp rock-like formations throughout the landscape. The terrain is filled with various objects from the game's past as well as bygone architecture from before the war started. The sky above the landscape swirls with purples and pinks, and is dotted by a myriad of stars. The [[Banlands|Nil Zone]] now acts as a prison to entities who pose a threat to the balance of the Meta, with the [[Rift Walker (Story)|Rift Walker]] banishing those who he deems dangerous enough. The [[Null Guardian]] is tasked with supervision of the [[Banlands|Outer Nil Zone]], acting as the warden to those banished there.{{InlineQuote|Anyway uhh, welcome to the edge of the [[Nil Zone]] where 'handsome' here cleans up the washed up talent.|[[Narrator (Story)|Narrator]] in the beginning cutscene of [[Banlands]]}} Within the [[Banlands|Nil Zone]] exists the Temple of Exo, a structure connected to [[Lord Exo]] in some way. While not explicitly stated, the Temple of Exo is heavily implied to be where the events of [[Blind Faith]] take place, where [[Lord Exo]] was freed from the [[God Cube]]. According to the [[Narrator (Story)|Narrator]], the temple is a place where [[God Cube]] shards can be merged together into a larger whole, as the [[Children of Exo]] were lead the temple, making the [[Narrator (Story)|Narrator]] coalesce their collected fragments together.{{InlineQuote|You USED me, to bring you to the Temple of Exo! THEN you scheming JERKS made me put together your [[God Cube|GOD CUBE]] PIECES before throwing me to the Executioner!|[[Narrator (Story)|Narrator]] in the beginning cutscene of [[Banlands]]}} It was discovered by the [[T.D.S. Organization]] that the [[Banlands|Nil Zone]] is the "''space between realms''" that transcends the fabric of the [[Meta]], being the medium that interdimensional portals use to connect to other realms.{{InlineQuote|I knew it! There had to be something out there! I theorized that if portals act as tunnels to other realms, then what kind of space were we tunneling through?|[[Nerd Duck (Narrator)|Nerd Duck]] on Wave 5 ([[Outpost 16]])}} Special, unstable energy exists within the [[Banlands|Nil Zone]] that was created because of the war.{{InlineQuote|The [[Nil Zone]]'s unstable energy was created from endless eons of war.|[[Marcellus]] on Wave 27 ([[Blind Faith]])}} It is due to this energy that the [[Banlands|Nil Zone]] is able to corrupt life,{{InlineQuote|The chaotic energy in the [[Nil Zone]] was beginning to corrupt the few that remained, including myself...|[[Narrator (Narrator)|Narrator]] on Wave 21 ([[The Narratorium]])}} and replicate forms of life from other realms, as seen during the events of [[Outpost 16]].{{InlineQuote|Those [[Nil Zone]] creatures may be more sensitive to the corruption than we are. As the energy expands outwards, it might be violently ripping through your bodies and replicating your DNA into them!|[[Nerd Duck (Narrator)|Nerd Duck]] on Wave 7 ([[Outpost 16]])}} {{Clear}} ===Void=== {{LocationInfobox |title = Void |image = PlaceC.png |aliases = Mother{{InlineQuote|The child was not the Void. The child called it Mother. What she did know was that she was the Void Caster, the daughter of the Void.|[[Void Caster]]'s description in its [[Logbooks|Logbook]]}} |inhabitants = The [[Void Caster]] |located=Beneath the foundations of the '''Old World'''{{InlineQuote|For the first and final time, they drove it deep down into the foundations of the world, into a dark so total its song could never be heard again.|[[Void Caster]]'s description in its [[Logbooks|Logbook]]}} }} The Void is a primordial force that has existed alongside [[Two X]] and [[Lord Exo]] before the '''Old World''' even had a recognizable form.{{InlineQuote|Before there was anything to call the Old World, the Void was already waiting in the dark.|[[Void Caster]]'s description in its [[Logbooks|Logbook]]}} Unlike [[Two X]] and [[Lord Exo]], it is hard to gauge whether the Void is a sentient intelligence of its own, acting more as a force of nature.{{InlineQuote|It cannot be considered a place or a creature, but something else entirely. It is a quiet hunger that lurks beneath the notice of every being, the presence that can be felt when nothing is around. The pale flora that blooms in a place where nothing exists is where it finds its peace. It is of one mind, though it wears a thousand faces. One could call it an incurable infection.|[[Void Caster]]'s description in its [[Logbooks|Logbook]]}} This is corroborated by the fact that the [[Void Caster]] exists as an agent of the Void to manifest its will. The Void was sealed away by [[Two X]] and [[Lord Exo]] eons ago, as they could not destroy it. Though, this could not stop the Void's influence entirely, as it still managed to spawn the [[Void Caster]]. During the war in the '''Old World''', the [[Void Caster]] was promised by [[Lord Exo]] that if she helped him fight [[Two X]], he would ensure that the Void can inhabit the world. When [[Lord Exo]] was defeated, [[Two X]] focused his attention on hunting down any traces of the Void that remained in the [[Banlands|Nil Zone]].{{InlineQuote|When Lord Exo was sealed away, Two X turned his attention to the Void itself, hunting it throughout the Nil Zone. So the Void slunk back into the depths from which it was sealed, and the Void Caster went to the one place Two X would never follow. Straight into the heart of the Void itself. Even he would not set foot there. Even though a God cannot be killed, there are things worse than death that the Void was patiently waiting to do.|[[Void Caster]]'s description in its [[Logbooks|Logbook]]}} But yet, that was not enough to completely eradicate it, as the Void still managed to destroy realms created by [[Two X]].{{InlineQuote|Many of the Odd were from realms the Void had fully consumed.|[[Odd]]'s description in its [[Logbooks|Logbook]]}} After [[Lord Exo]] was freed, the [[Void Caster]] still remembered the promise they made eons ago, and quickly mobilized her troops to expedite the process of having the Void consume realms, causing the Void Rifts that appeared throughout the [[Meta]].{{InlineQuote|The Meta exists everywhere across the entire Nil Zone, but it was not until the Rift Walker fell and the realms began to destabilize that the seams gave. Holes formed that connected the two worlds, and through the thinnest of those tears the Void crept out once more. In the barrens of the Nil Zone, where there was once life, a single lone flower blossomed from the earth.|[[Void Caster]]'s description in its [[Logbooks|Logbook]]}} {{Clear}} ==Trivia== *[[Lord Exo]] is visually represented imprisoned inside the [[God Cube]] as sitting on a throne within the [[Nil Zone]]. **This place made its first appearance in Tower Defense Simulator in the [[Lunar Overture Event]], being the event lobby. *The portal that the [[Children of Exo]] were trying to open in [[Failed Gateway]] was their attempt at establishing a connection to the [[Nil Zone]]. *The "''Nil Zone''" is an exonym given to the '''Old World''' by the [[T.D.S. Organization]]."''We've named that space the 'Nil Zone'. I never thought a place like that could exist.''" — [[Professor V]] on Wave 5 ([[Outpost 16]]) ==Notes== {{StoryNavBox}}
